Conducted original empirical research on financial literacy among Bangalore's gig workers — with findings published on SSRN while still in high school.
:::

## Abstract

Gig workers form a rapidly growing segment of Bangalore's urban workforce, yet their financial literacy levels and implications for economic security remain under-studied. This paper presents an empirical analysis of financial knowledge, savings behaviour, and access to formal financial services among gig-economy workers in Bangalore. The findings reveal significant gaps in financial literacy that correlate with income volatility and limited access to structured financial planning — highlighting the need for targeted financial education interventions in India's informal economy.

## What I Did

::: {.project-section}
<ul class="star-list">
<li><strong>Situation:</strong> Bangalore's gig economy is expanding rapidly, but little empirical research exists on the financial literacy of workers in this sector.</li>
<li><strong>Task:</strong> Design and conduct a rigorous empirical study, analyse the data, and publish findings in an academic forum.</li>
<li><strong>Action:</strong> Developed a research framework, collected and analysed survey data from gig workers across Bangalore, and wrote up findings with statistical rigour.</li>
<li><strong>Result:</strong> Paper published on SSRN: *"Financial Literacy in Bangalore Gig Workers: An Empirical Analysis."*</li>
</ul>
:::
